steps.what: Read the actual funding call and verify eligibility, required sections and submission constraints
Define the actual research question, methods, work packages and cost assumptions for the grant
Assemble the required grant sections, institutional facts, budget tables and supplied references in the call's structure
Write the grant narrative explaining the actual research rationale, methods, contribution and feasibility

loop.purpose: Suggest grant prose from the sociologist's actual outline and evidence
loop.input: Checked call structure, actual research/budget outline and supplied source passages
loop.output: Draft rationale, methods and feasibility prose with source pointers
loop.check: Sociologist checks every factual claim, reference, proposed commitment and number against real inputs in s5
loop.stop: Two drafts; unsupported material is removed and remaining writing stays with the sociologist
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed template handles s3, but expressing the actual research argument requires semantic writing

steps.what: Verify the complete grant's scientific argument, citations, budget and commitments and correct the actual working application
Save the ordinary working grant in the same document workspace

tasks.design: Assemble the call's fixed fields and real budget tables from {SPREADSHEET} into {DOCS}. A bounded writing loop proposes prose from the actual research outline; the sociologist checks the full scientific argument and every factual commitment before saving a working application.
tasks.previous_blocker: Call structures require repeated assembly and a new expression of an actual research plan.
tasks.enabler_now: Fixed templates handle exact fields while a bounded writing assistant can suggest outline-based prose.
tasks.still_hard: A credible research contribution, feasible methods and defensible commitments require the researcher's judgment.
tasks.human_edge: The sociologist knows what the project can actually establish and deliver.

ambition.what: Consider more suitable funding calls without manufacturing new research claims.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: grant templates can assemble fixed fields and bounded prose drafting can support an actual research outline, with substantive human verification.

assumptions: Boundary is grant writing through a saved working application. Actual institutional sign-off, funder-portal submission and financial commitment are separate work; they require their actual authority after the exact final application exists and a separate gated submission. No invented author self-approval is added here.

s1 reads the actual call. s2 counts producing the real research and cost outline; institutional facts and references come from actual existing records, selected and checked here rather than a new free dataset.
Test existing call templates and budget exports first; existing assembly support earns zero new saving. s3 prices only actual repeated manual assembly.

s4 retains12.5 of25 narrative units, s5 retains19 full verification/correction units and upkeep includes2 additional exception-writing units; unsupported citations and claims are removed rather than accepted from model memory.

tasks.short: Develop research-based approaches to groups' problems

steps.what: Clarify the actual group's problem and examine the available context with the group or project participants
Read the actual sociology and related research findings and assess their methods and population relevance
Develop and compare specific approaches to the group's problems against the actual evidence and practical constraints
Write the actual working options paper used by the project group, including evidence links and conditions for each approach
Save the ordinary working options paper in the current project document

tasks.design: Use an options-paper layout in {DOCS} with source-reference fields from {OTHER}, the research reference manager. Keep the actual group discussion, research appraisal and development of approaches with the sociologist; the layout removes only repeated reference placement and section formatting.
tasks.previous_blocker: The actual options paper can require repeated source-reference insertion and layout work.
tasks.enabler_now: Native reference fields and document sections can remove those assembly actions.
tasks.still_hard: Research findings can transfer poorly across groups, institutions and power relationships.
tasks.human_edge: The sociologist relates evidence to the group's actual problem without treating a generic intervention as established.

ambition.what: Compare more adequately supported approaches within the actual project.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: reference-manager fields and document layouts can reduce options-paper assembly while sociological applicability judgment remains human.

assumptions: Boundary is an actual project that uses a written options paper. Do not add this paper to an informal advisory conversation where nobody keeps or reads it. Implementation authority, publication and any actual send are separate final-version actions.
s1 counts the real group discussion and context capture. s2 reads and checks the actual research; no free structured problem or evidence dataset is assumed.

research_questions: Which reference insertion actions remain manual after native document tools?

tasks.short: Observe group interactions and assess change needs

steps.what: Observe actual group interactions and role affiliations and capture contemporaneous observation facts
Write the actual field notes used for later research analysis, separating observations from interpretations
Check the actual field notes and identify group problems, progress and possible need for additional change
outputs: checked field notes and change-needs interpretation

steps.what: Save the ordinary field notes in the same research workspace
inputs: checked field notes and change-needs interpretation

tasks.design: Reuse only the existing session identifier and headings in {DOCS}, with {OTHER} denoting the actual field-observation setting and research session index. Keep live observation, factual note writing and interpretation with the sociologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual field notes can repeat the session reference and protocol headings.
tasks.enabler_now: A native session-linked note can fill those existing metadata fields without observing or classifying people.
tasks.still_hard: Interactions, role meanings and the researcher's presence affect what observations support.
tasks.human_edge: The sociologist distinguishes observable events from interpretation and contextual inference.

ambition.what: No automated group monitoring or individual classification.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: existing session metadata can populate field-note headers while observation and sociological interpretation remain human.

assumptions: Boundary is an actual research observation episode with real field notes used for later analysis, not a new report added after conversation. No audio recording, transcript or structured observation feed is assumed.
s1 counts real-time factual capture. s2 counts actual field-note writing and s3 counts interpretation; there is no free clean source produced elsewhere.

role.altitude: Research design, group observation and sociological interpretation remain human; explicit application assembly and actual repeated document fields can shrink.
reach: Work with actual project and funding staff on call fields and research-document provenance.
skills_to_grow: Clear separation of observation and inference
role.ambitious_version: A sociologist who develops traceable proposals and group approaches with less repeated assembly while retaining scientific judgment and real release authority.
